study type: Nested study within a prospective cohort study
exposure: Placental pathologic findings (maternal vascular malperfusion, fetal vascular malperfusion, ascending intrauterine infections, inflammatory lesions, chorangiosis)
cohort: The study included 121 singleton pregnant women diagnosed with severe COVID-19.
finding: Maternal vascular malperfusion was the most prevalent placental feature in patients with severe COVID-19, and chorangiosis (a type of inflammatory lesion) was associated with poor perinatal outcomes.
